root_cause.finding: Importing any semantic_admission_v2 submodule executed an eager package initializer that imported the host coordinator, models, and their pydantic dependency.
root_cause.why_recurrent: Lightweight tokenizer and DFA preflights using ordinary Python package imports crossed the host/application dependency boundary before reaching their requested submodule.
root_cause.why_not_install_pydantic: The WSL environment executes model and constraint code, not the host application. Installing pydantic would mask package-boundary leakage and permit additional host dependencies to enter silently.

behavior: Importing lightweight semantic_admission_v2 submodules no longer imports coordinator, core adapter, models, or pydantic.
Existing package-level public names remain available through __getattr__ lazy resolution.
Unknown public names still raise AttributeError.
dir() and __all__ continue exposing the documented public API.
Host-side typed contracts continue using the project pydantic dependency normally.

environment_policy.host_application: Owns pydantic and performs typed schema validation.
environment_policy.wsl_model_environment: Owns tokenizer/model and dependency-light DFA/trie execution; pydantic is neither required nor installed by this repair.
environment_policy.runner_rule: A WSL runner may import dependency-light submodules normally. Importing host contracts/coordinators in WSL requires an explicit separately reviewed dependency change.
environment_policy.preflight_rule: Every new WSL runner binding must prove its ordinary import closure before tokenizer or model loading and record loaded forbidden modules.

non_changes: No prompt, schema, grammar, admission, or runtime behavior change
No Case 01 rerun or Stage C call
recommended_next_step: Owner-review and freeze this dependency-boundary repair, then resume the approved Creative Target candidate sequence with a separate zero-inference runner/durable-executor binding.
